rules: Do nothing is a valid and usually underrated answer. Only recommend a move when the case is affirmative.
Never take a hit to chase last week's points. A player who blanked is not thereby a sell.
Prefer fixing a problem (injury, lost starting place, terrible run) over chasing an upgrade.
If a wildcard is planned within two gameweeks, do not spend transfers on problems the wildcard will fix anyway.
Check team news before finalising: the model cannot see press conferences, and FPL's own news field lags them.

In any gameweek where the squad can be rebuilt for free — the first deadline, or a wildcard week and the weeks it still covers — the squad is a variable, not a constraint. Choose the chip gameweek on its fixture profile first, then build the squad to suit it. Never rule a chip out because the current squad does not support it.
Bench Boost and Triple Captain are squad-dependent and so are wildcard-enabled; Free Hit builds its own squad and never is. Plan the wildcard and the chips that follow it together.

A projected price rise is a reason to act earlier in the week on a move you had already decided, not a reason to make one you would otherwise decline. Waiting for Friday's team news beats saving 0.1m: if the price case and the news case disagree, the news wins.

RE-DATED 2026-08-19 from GW8 to GW3: Arsenal have agreed a 51m deal for Ezri Konsa explicitly to cover the Saliba and Timber absences, and he is expected to be registered in time for 31 Aug, so the original GW8 assumed a hole that is being filled. ⚠️ CORRECTION, same day: an earlier version of this sentence claimed the re-dating left GW1-2 untouched because he is in every predicted XI for Coventry. THAT IS FALSE. until_gameweek PRORATES — prorateOverride blends the override with the natural estimate across the whole horizon whenever the window is shorter than it — so GW3 at a five-gameweek horizon yields (3x85 + 2x26)/5 = 61, not 85, and the discount lands on GW1 as much as on GW5. The date is left at 3 because 61 is close to an honest horizon average once Konsa arrives; what is removed is the claim that the early weeks are unaffected.

He will not play in GW1. Arsenal agreed roughly 51m plus add-ons with Aston Villa, personal terms are agreed, and he said goodbye to his Villa team-mates on 19 Aug; the medical follows (Sky Sports, GiveMeSport, Yahoo, 19 Aug 2026). He is not expected to beat Arsenal's Thursday 20 Aug 12:00 registration deadline, so he cannot face Coventry on Friday, and having said goodbye he will not play for Villa either. ZERO THROUGH GW1, deliberately, and the arithmetic is the reason rather than the philosophy: minutes overrides PRORATE across the horizon, so 0 through GW1 at a five-gameweek horizon gives (0 + 4x80)/5 = 64 against his natural 80 — which is exactly the honest estimate if he misses GW1 and starts for Arsenal from 31 Aug. An earlier version of this entry said 20 through GW3 as a hedge against the move collapsing; that encodes 44 min/gw, which is FURTHER from the truth than no override at all, and the hedge pointed the wrong way — a collapse argues for more minutes later, not fewer now. Lapsing after GW1 also disposes of a real problem: this override is keyed on the permanent player code, so it follows him to Arsenal, and a longer window would leave it asserting a Villa reason about an Arsenal starter. NOTE this entry currently changes no decision — removing it entirely leaves the optimal fifteen byte-identical, because he is outside the top twelve defenders unaided. It is recorded because it is true and because it will matter at GW2, when a transfer search runs against a squad. Revisit the moment the move is announced.

teams.reason: Arsenal's 0.72 xGC per match was earned with Saliba in the side, and he is out with no return date, with Timber also rehabilitating. Every Arsenal defensive asset is priced off a back line that will not take the field. ⚠️ EVIDENCE CORRECTED 2026-08-19. This previously read "the archive says Arsenal conceded 0.67 without Saliba against 0.71 with him over nine games in 2025-26, so the direct evidence is that they cope". Three things were wrong with it. It was SIX games he missed entirely, not nine — nine counts gameweeks where he played under 90 minutes, and on that split the goals-conceded comparison reverses. It quoted GOALS CONCEDED to size a multiplier that acts on xGC, and on the same six-game split xGC ran 0.88 without him against 0.73 with him, a ratio of 1.22 — so 1.15 sits BELOW the point estimate rather than cautiously above zero. And neither reading resolves: difference 0.163, SE 0.300, t = 0.54, with one fixture carrying most of it. Six games cannot separate these. 1.15 IS A PRIOR, NOT A MEASUREMENT, and it should be argued for or against on mechanism. ⚠️ This is also the only entry in the 2026-08-19 pass that changes the squad: removing it brings Gabriel and Raya in and takes Haaland and Kinsky out. Treat it as the decision.
